title: Present tense and -te chai
focus: Simple present for ami / tumi / o (ami khai, tumi khao, o khay); wanting to do things with -te chai (ami khete chai).
body:
# Present tense and -te chai

Bengali verbs change their ending depending on **who** does the action. They don't change for gender: **o** means both "he" and "she".

The simple present covers what you do in general or as a habit ("I eat rice", "she goes every day").

## The pattern

| Person | Ending | khaoa (eat) | jaoa (go) | chaoa (want) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ami (I) | -i | ami khai | ami jai | ami chai |
| tumi (you) | -o | tumi khao | tumi jao | tumi chao |
| o (he/she) | -y / -e | o khay | o jay | o chay |

## Wanting to do something: -te chai

To say "want to do X", put the **-te form** of the verb before **chai / chao / chay**. Only chai changes for the person. The -te form never changes.

| Verb | -te form | "I want to..." |
|---|---|---|
| khaoa (eat) | khete | ami khete chai |
| jaoa (go) | jete | ami jete chai |
| pora (read) | porte | ami porte chai |

## Examples

- **tumi khao**: you eat
- **o jay**: he/she goes
- **ami cha khai**: I drink tea (lit. "I eat tea")
- **tumi jol chao**: you want water
- **beral-ta bhat khay**: the cat eats rice
- **ami boi pori**: I read books
- **tumi jete chao**: you want to go
- **o aaj jete chay**: he/she wants to go today
- **beral-ta ghumote chay**: the cat wants to sleep
- **ami khete chai, kintu khabar-ta gorom**: I want to eat, but the food is hot

The object goes **before** the verb: *ami cha khai* = "I tea eat".

## Common mistakes

1. **Conjugating both verbs.** It's *ami khete chai*, not ~~ami khai chai~~. Only *chai* takes the person ending.
2. **Using a separate "drink" verb.** In Kolkata you *khao* tea and water: *cha khai*, *jol khai*.
